Author: Krishan Pahal
Bench: Krishan Pahal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 83
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 59657 of 2022
Applicant :- Lalit
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Anjani Kumar Raghuvanshi,Kumar Dhananjay

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today.
Taken on record.

3. Heard Shri Anjani Kumar Raghuvanshi, learned counsel for the applicant and learned counsel for the informant as well as Shri Yogesh Mishra learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
4.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 216 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 328, 376B, 376(2)
I.P.C. & 5(g)/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Kasna, District Gautambhuddha Nagar, during the pendency of trial.
5. As per prosecution story, the co-accused person, Arjun is said to have enticed away the minor grand daughter of the informant aged 14 years 6 months on 14.09.2022 at about 10.00 am.

Learned Lalit vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20688201/

sentences.text: counsel for the applicant has stated that he is falsely implicated in the case.
He is the elder brother of the named accused person Arjun.
Learned counsel has stated that the victim is a consenting party.

To buttress his argument, learned counsel has placed reliance on the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. whereby she has not levelled any kind of allegations against anybody and there is no whisper against the applicant.

Learned counsel has stated that after a period of 38 days,
the statement of victim has been recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and the name of the applicant has been introduced.

Learned counsel has stated that in the said statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. victim had stated that she had left her house peeved by scolding of her partents and she met the co-accused Arjun and she was taken to secluded place by him and has been sexually assaulted by the applicant as well as Arjun.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case, owing to his relationship with the co-accused person Arjun as he is real younger brother.
The applicant is a married person.

Learned counsel has stated that earlier on similar allegations, another FIR was lodged by the father of the victim at FIR No. 386 of 2022 whereby the statement of victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

The victim had categorically stated in the said statement that she had gone out of her sweet will with the brother of the applicant and her age was 17 years and she had not levelled any kind of allegations of sexual assault against the co-accused Arjun.
Learned counsel has stated that it was also stated in the said statement that she wanted to marry the brother of the applicant Arjun.
Learned counsel has stated that the age of the victim is more than 18 years as his self evident from her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. in FIR No. 386 of 2022.
But in her statement recorded in this case, she has mentioned her age to be 15 years.
Learned counsel has stated that the said statements are self-contradictory and cannot be believed and applicant is not named in the FIR and is entitled for bail.
The FIR is also delayed by about 10 days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 23.10.2022.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant- Lalit involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.

sentences.text: (ii). The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
10.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
